documentation.rationale: Identity half is present: the VIN decodes cleanly, the listing reports a clean title and Carfax, and the Carfax-consistent odometer reading is quoted. Maintenance half is thin: 14 Carfax service records are referenced but not shown, plugs are dated 2019, and there is nothing on coolant, transaxle oil, oil consumption or the underbody. Capture was incomplete, so the full Carfax and videos may exist on the page.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight, consistent paint, a good-looking top with glass window, clean wheels, a tidy stock engine bay and good fabric seats. The steering wheel shows wear. One fault is disclosed: a stuck recirculation door with reduced fan speed. The underside is mostly unseen, and it is a Colorado car.

price_value.rationale: The $6,000 bid is early. The expected hammer for a 30k-mile 5-speed lands near the $13.8-14.5k fair-value band. A small HVAC repair and the unknown age-related service keep this at roughly fair value.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual, Toyota-simple and very likely within the ideal budget band. It is easy to resell in 6-24 months and is a genuine driver's car, though it is not one of Jason's named primary bridge candidates.

logistics.rationale: Castle Rock, CO is a fly-and-drive distance. A PPI is possible near Denver but must be arranged with the seller before the Oct 22 close. CA smog feasibility depends on the emissions label.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Low-mile, one-family, stock 5-speed with the 2003+ glass-window top. Silver is a common colour and there is no LSD.

ppi_focus: Lift inspection of the underbody coolant pipes and clamps for corrosion or seepage, plus a cooling-system pressure test
Jack points, rockers, front subframe and rear suspension mounts for Colorado road-salt corrosion
OBD-II scan for P0420/P0421, misfire, ABS and EPS codes; listen for manifold pre-cat rattle
Oil level and condition check, spark plug wells, and evidence of oil burning (tailpipe soot, plug fouling)

Diagnose the HVAC recirculation door and blower speed

Tire DOT codes and brake caliper function after age
what_would_change_verdict: Clean lift photos or a PPI showing a dry, rust-free underbody and sound coolant pipes would raise condition and documentation.
Carfax entries showing coolant, brake fluid and transaxle service, plus a low oil-consumption record, would raise documentation.
Rot at the jack points or subframe, a leaking coolant pipe, or evidence of oil burning would move it down sharply.
Refusal of a PPI or more photos before close would lower logistics and documentation.
A hammer well above the ~$14k fair-value band would lower price value.
evidence.mission_note: A stock, low-mile 5-speed Toyota roadster fits the enthusiast-bridge brief: a manual with a point of view, Corolla-simple to own and easy to resell. It should still not be bought unseen given the Colorado underbody and oil-consumption unknowns. It is a credible alternative to the Z3 3.0i, not one of the named primary candidates.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly as a 2003 MR2, and the listing reports a clean Colorado title, a clean Carfax with 2 owners in one family, and ~30k miles consistent with Carfax's 29,989 reading. It is a true 5-speed. Photos show a stock, straight car with consistent silver paint, a good glass-window top, a clean engine bay and good seats. They also show a worn steering wheel. One fault is disclosed: a stuck recirculation door with reduced fan speed. Maintenance evidence amounts to a reference to 14 Carfax entries, spark plugs in 2019, and a battery and tires in 2026 per the seller; no receipts or Carfax pages were captured. The model-defining items remain open: no oil-consumption data, no OBD scan or pre-cat check, and only a single partial underside photo on a Colorado car. The coolant pipes, jack points and subframe mounts are unseen. Expected hammer sits near the ~$14k fair-value band, well above the current $6,000 early bid.
